text: Chattahoochee State Park was a public recreation area situated in the extreme southeast corner of Alabama, managed by the government of Houston County, Alabama. The park spanned 596 acres (241 ha) along Irwin's Mill Creek on the Florida-Alabama border. It closed after much of the park was destroyed by Hurricane Michael in 2018. Land adjacent to the park was the site of an 1818 skirmish during the First Seminole War. The state park was developed in the 1930s by members of the Civilian Conservation Corps, who constructed a natural stone dam to form the 23-acre (9.3 ha) CC Pond and built the park’s dirt roads; remnants such as chimneys from the CCC workers' camp were once visible. Most of the park’s facilities and trees were damaged by Hurricane Michael in October 2018, leading to its permanent closure due to the state’s inability to fund clearing, repair, and rebuilding efforts. In 2022, slow progress was being made toward reopening the park, with hopes of having it reopened by 2024.
